messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY P1 -> PrimeApex (VPC) pa-prod-1: KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse detected for prefixes 'usr:' and 'session:'. p50 latency ↑ 320ms, errors 5%. Auto-escalation to on-call. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prefetch

alice: ack. On-call ben, you got the page?

ben: I'm on it. Paging into channel and pulling metrics. cc @carla @mike @eva

carla: saw the alert. Quick question — any recent config changes for pa-prod-1 or tenant-level prefetch?

mike: primeapex support says customer traffic spiked after a campaign around 19:10 UTC. They saw increased 5xx and slow responses from our endpoint. No direct API schema changes reported.

ben: running quick metrics call
```
rbctl metrics get --tenant primeapex --pool pa-prod-1 --metric kv_cache.hitrate --prefix 'usr:' --window 10m
```

ben: output: hitrate: 2.1% (10m avg). Baseline yesterday ~84%. Prefetch rate spiked ~150x.

carla: that smells like a prefetch or key churn storm. If prefetch queue floods, other prefixes get evicted -> global hit-rate collapse.

ben: checking prefetch queue length and prefetch worker logs
```
rbctl inspect prefetch --pool pa-prod-1 --tail 200
# logs show repetitive prefetch requests for session:* from tenant primeapex starting 2055006000
```

mike: customer-side: they confirmed they rolled out a client-side caching change that accidentally bubbled TTL down to 0 causing every request to generate a new session key.

eva: notifying PrimeApex CSM and legal that we're investigating. Customer impacted: yes, degraded latency and some failed requests. No evidence of data leak.

ben: mitigation proposal: 1) throttle/disable tenant prefetch for primeapex 2) temporarily increase KV cache allocation for pa-prod-1 3) apply a prefix isolation policy to protect core prefixes from churn. Anyone object?

carla: agree. Order: disable prefetch first (fastest), then resize cache if we still see hit-rate problems.

ben: executing disable prefetch (will be quick to revert)
```
rbctl cache prefetch disable --tenant primeapex --pool pa-prod-1 --reason "incident: prefetch storm"
```

deploy-bot: config-change: prefetch disabled for tenant=primeapex pool=pa-prod-1 by ben at 2055010200 :white_check_mark:

ben: monitoring metrics now.

(5m later)

ben: preliminary: hit-rate climbed to 46%, p50 latency down 90ms, errors trending down. Still below baseline.

carla: let's provision an extra 2GB KV for the pool while we work through root cause so other tenants not impacted. This is a controlled, temporary increase.

ben: resizing pool cache now
```
rbctl pool resize --pool pa-prod-1 --kv-cache +2GB --reason "incident mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: pool resize scheduled for pa-prod-1 by ben at 2055011400 — applying...

(30s)

deploy-bot: pool resize completed: pa-prod-1 kv-cache increased by 2GB

ben: metrics after resize: hit-rate 72%, p50 latency back near baseline, errors <0.5%. Customer reports responsiveness improving.

mike: customer confirmed improvement on their end. They rolled back the faulty client change on their staging; will schedule safer rollouts.

eva: relaying to PrimeApex: mitigation applied, asking for follow-up plan and postmortem. They asked for an RCA and whether we can add guardrails to prevent tenant prefetch storms in future.

carla: action items: - temporary prefetch disabled (ben) - pool cache bumped +2GB (ben) - schedule permanent prefix-isolation policy for pa-prod-1 to protect critical prefixes (carla) - add an alert when per-tenant prefetch rate > X/s (sre_lead) - discuss tenant-side best practices with CSM (eva)

sre_lead: noted. I'll own the alerting task and coordinate a postmortem. Please add logs/metrics snapshot to the incident ticket.

ben: leaving a short runbook blurb in-case this recurs: 
"When tenant prefetch rate spikes and overall KV hit-rate collapses: 1) disable tenant prefetch; 2) increase pool cache if latency critical; 3) enable per-tenant prefix caps; 4) reach out to customer; 5) plan longer-term guardrails."

alice: acknowledged. Handoff to night on-call (carla will lead during her shift). ben — please confirm when you handoff.

ben: handing off at 2055013500 to carla. Current state: prefetch disabled, pool +2GB, hit-rate 74%, errors down to 0.2%. No further customer-visible regressions.

carla: thanks — taking it through the night. Scheduling follow-up meeting 2pm UTC tomorrow with PrimeApex.

sre_lead: please ensure incident ticket contains: timeline, commands executed, metrics pre/post, and owner for alert task. I'll open postmortem template.

eva: sharing notes with PrimeApex and confirming no billing anomalies. They appreciated the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

ben: adding final note — no code rollback required. Re-enabling prefetch should be a coordinated change after prefix isolation and throttling are in place.

incident-bot: Incident P1 (PrimeApex pa-prod-1) status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident channel will remain open until postmortem created.

carla: closing logs for now, will update ticket with full timeline. Good job team. :rocket:
